sector_model: payment network: revenue growth, adjusted EPS, FCF after SBC and buybacks versus net debt; bank ratios not applicable
thesis: Mastercard Inc. (NYSE: MA), global payment network, mega cap. Q3 2026 (release 2026-10-29): net revenue 9.807B (+14%, currency-neutral +14%), payment network +11%, value-added services +18.5%, GAAP EPS 5.28, adjusted EPS 5.31 (+21%), cross-border volume +11%, switched transactions +9%; Q3 buybacks 3.0B. TTM GAAP EPS 19.11, TTM FCF about 16.1B. At 661.19 (2026-11-13 close, 52-week 464.52-681.99, about 3% below the high) P/E is 34.6x, FCF yield 2.8% (2.7% after SBC), dividend yield 0.5%, net debt about 13.9B after a 5.0B note issue in June and the 1.4B BVNK stablecoin acquisition in August. Quality is high and growth is steady; the question is price, not business. The market is paying a premium multiple for durable mid-teens growth and buybacks.
counterthesis: A 34.6x trailing multiple and 2.8% FCF yield leave little margin: a deceleration to high single digits or an interchange or surcharge regulatory change would compress it. Regulation (U.S. merchant litigation, UK and EU interchange cases, Credit Card Competition Act style proposals), stablecoin and account-to-account disruption, tariffs on cross-border travel and debt-funded buybacks (equity only 6.8B) are risks. Litigation accrual dropped to 262M, so earlier charges may reverse the tailwind. It is also a large holding in broad US index funds, so exposure duplicates the core allocation.
invalidation: Thesis breaks if net revenue growth falls below about 10% for several quarters, cross-border volume turns negative, a binding interchange cap is enacted, or a large unaccrued settlement hits.
